name: Spades
tagline: Partners bid their tricks. Spades are always trump. Watch your bags.

rulesSummary: Partners sit across: your two bids added up are your side's contract.
Three players: everyone for themselves, 17 cards each (one card is out of play). The 2♣ leads (the 3♣ if the 2♣ is out).
Each trick over your bid costs 10 instead of being a bag. Anyone who falls to −200 loses, and the leader wins.
Three pairs, partners across: your two bids added up are your side's contract. Two packs without the 2♦s, 17 cards each. If two identical cards land on one trick, the later one wins.
Each player bids how many tricks they'll take. Bid 0 for nil: you aim to take no tricks.
Follow suit if you can; if not, play anything. Spades are always trump: the highest spade wins, or else the highest card of the suit led.
Spades can't be led until one has been played, unless you hold only spades.
Make your bid: 10 for each trick bid, plus 1 for each extra trick (a bag). Miss it: lose 10 for each trick bid.
Nil scores +100 if you take no tricks, −100 if you take any. A nil player's tricks don't help the partner's bid, but they count as bags. Every 10 bags costs 100.
Blind nil (partners only; it can be turned off in the lobby): a side 100 or more behind may bid nil before looking, for ±200. Your partner gives you 2 cards, then you give 2 back.
When anyone reaches the target (500 unless changed), the highest score wins. If the top scores are level, play another hand.
